The GPS track contains two off-route segments: 14:10–14:13 adding 1.63 km (up to 816 m off route) and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.83 km (up to 1553 m off route) — both are unexempted deviations unless an exemption applies.

The rider never named the Beach Road location; the driver admits in his own statement that 'I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road', so the stop location was chosen by the driver without telling the rider beforehand, and its extra_km is not exempt under RD-3(b).

The 4 min 10 s stop at 14:20–14:24 was 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, i.e. well off the optimal route, and on a metered RydeTAXI the metered waiting units of $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) stand, but that waiting time does not license the extra distance driven.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.99 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
Traffic screen: the case is a metered RydeTAXI trip whose distance enters the fare [F9][RD-2]. The GPS record shows two off-route segments, F4 (+1.63 km) and F5 (+2.83 km), so each is reviewed separately for exemption [F4][F5][RD-1].

For F4 the exemption is settled by code: an LTA incident (accident 13:52, Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed) sits 30 m from the optimal route on the replaced stretch, reported before the 14:10 segment start [F18][F4][RD-4]. Orchard Road was additionally at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) at 14:00–14:10, which corroborates but does not itself exempt [F15][RD-4]. F4 is therefore exempt and its 1.63 km is not refundable.

For F5 the code finds no qualifying incident, so the exemption could only come from rider consent under RD-5 [F5][RD-4]. The driver named a route — "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" at 14:01 — and the rider answered "Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" at 14:02, both before the F5 segment started at 14:17 [F10][F11][RD-5]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F13]. Consent covers the route the driver actually named, but the record shows a different destination: the driver's own statement admits he chose the 7-Eleven "I know on Beach Road", a stop far off the Cavenagh corridor, where the car stood stationary 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 about 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, and the F5 trace reaches up to 1553 m off the optimal route [F14][F2][F5]. A far, driver-chosen stop beyond the named corridor is exactly the "different destination" that ends the agreement's scope, so it cannot be read as consent to the whole of F5 [F14][F5][RD-5]. Driver-advocate D3, which sought to rest that leg on the rider's stop request, is withdrawn in rebuttal, and the rider never named the place ("a 7-Eleven on the way" only), so RD-3(a) does not exempt F5 — the whole way to a place the rider did not name is not excused [F11][F14][F5][RD-3]. F5 therefore counts.

Amount: the trip's own per-km rate is distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $13.14 ÷ 9.3 km = $1.41/km [F9][F6][RD-2]. Refundable mileage is the unexempted F5 extra_km only: 2.83 km × $1.41/km = $3.99 [F5][F9][RD-2]. The $7.58 excess-distance line is not refunded as such; only the unexempted segment's extra km is [F6][RD-2].

The metered waiting unit of $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) accrued during the rider-requested stop is chargeable on RydeTAXI and stands [F7][F2][RD-3]; the fare breakdown contains no unpublished add-on to strip out [F9][FARE-1].

No account flag: the code finds no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0; the single upheld dispute was a no-show), so the "repeated" precondition of RD-6 is not met even though this case is made out [F21][RD-6].
